mcat_description.short: Auditorium tensile structure is a custom-fabricated, large-span membrane roofing system using tensile fabric (PVC-coated polyester, PTFE, or HDPE) stretched over a steel cable-and-frame skeleton, designed to cover open-air or semi-open auditoriums, amphitheatres, and assembly venues without intermediate support columns.
mcat_description.long: An auditorium tensile structure is a pre-engineered, site-installed roofing and canopy solution that uses high-performance tensile membrane fabric — predominantly PVC-coated polyester (700–1050 GSM) or PTFE-coated fiberglass — held in constant tension over a galvanised or epoxy-coated structural steel framework. The system achieves large column-free spans, making it ideal for auditoriums, open-air theatres, sports arenas, and community halls where unobstructed sightlines and seating capacity are critical. Each structure is custom-designed to site dimensions, wind and rain load requirements, and aesthetic preferences, with shapes including saddle, dome, pyramid, hypar, and arch forms. Sold as a complete design-fabricate-install project, the structure is quoted per square foot of covered area and typically supplied by specialist tensile structure contractors across India.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, auditorium tensile structures are sold as custom-designed, site-installed projects by specialist tensile structure contractors — not as off-the-shelf products. PVC-coated polyester fabric (700–1050 GSM) is the dominant material in India due to its cost-effectiveness and availability, while PTFE-coated fiberglass is used for premium, long-life installations. Key fabric brands referenced in the Indian market include Sioen (European, used by South Indian contractors), Serge Ferrari, and Mehler. The structure consists of a steel framework (hot-dip galvanised or epoxy-coated hollow sections) with tensile fabric cut by CNC and joined by high-frequency welding, then pre-stressed using hydraulic jacks and turnbuckles. Shapes commonly specified in India include dome, saddle, arch, pyramid, and hypar. The market spans government/municipal auditoriums, educational institutions, sports facilities, and corporate campuses. Buyers typically approach contractors with site dimensions and load requirements; the contractor provides design, fabrication, and installation as a single turnkey scope. No single BIS standard governs tensile membrane structures in India specifically; structural design follows general IS codes for steel and wind/snow loads. The international reference standard for membrane structures is CECS 15:2004 (Chinese standard widely cited by global suppliers); European EN and ASCE standards are referenced for premium projects.
